title: ServiceManager Discovery and Binder Handles Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies servicemanager discovery and binder handles?
options: Use supported manager APIs and understand ServiceManager as policy-controlled discovery of endpoints, not the service implementation itself.
Assume a cached proxy cannot die
questions.answer: Use supported manager APIs and understand ServiceManager as policy-controlled discovery of endpoints, not the service implementation itself.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: ServiceManager executes the business logic for all registered Android services.
questions.explanation: Using reflection to fetch an undocumented service name couples an app to hidden policy, interfaces, transaction behavior, and release-specific availability.

questions.prompt: What does ServiceManager return to a successful lookup?
questions.answer: A Binder reference or handle that the client wraps in a proxy for the endpoint hosted elsewhere.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
